output: Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained immense popularity and demonstrated remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks. However, adapting these colossal models to specific downstream tasks remains a significant challenge, primarily due to their prohibitive size and computational demands. To address this, Parameter-efficient FineTuning (PeFT) methods have emerged as a dominant paradigm.

Chain-of-thought prompting (CoT; Wei et al., 2022; Nye et al., 2022) has become the de facto standard for achieving the best performance on large language model (LLM) benchmarks (OpenAI et al., 2024; Gemini Team et al., 2024). Nevertheless, it is widely held that CoT is primarily effective for tasks requiring symbolic reasoning. Sprague et al. (2025) reported that on the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark (Hendrycks et al., 2021), 95% of the performance gain from CoT is attributed to questions involving symbolic reasoning. Building on CoT, self-consistency (SC; Wang et al., 2023) further improves performance by sampling multiple CoT reasoning paths and selecting the most consistent answer.

Large Language Models (LLMs) advance a wide range of language tasks (Devlin et al., 2019; Radford et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2022b; Team et al., 2024; Touvron et al., 2023), but training on text alone leaves them weak in visual commonsense. Vision–Language Models (VLMs) jointly train on images and text (Alayrac et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023b, a; Li et al., 2023a; Dai et al., 2023; Cha et al., 2024), improving visually grounded abilities.

Traditional spoken dialogue systems are typically half-duplex, alternating turns between user and system. While simple, this design struggles to capture the natural dynamics of conversation and often introduces latency. Full-duplex dialogue systems, in contrast, allow simultaneous listening and speaking, enabling more fluid and natural interactions.

Text embedding models encode textual inputs into vector spaces. These models enable efficient semantic representation and matching, thus serving as a foundation for many applications involving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In these tasks, candidate documents are typically segmented into smaller chunks to facilitate efficient processing. However, since documents often exhibit a narrative or logical flow, the meaning of each chunk is highly dependent on its surrounding context. This highlights the need for text embeddings that capture broader contextual information to enable context-aware retrieval.

This paper compiles evidence from a broad range of literature to support the argument that Big AI is accelerating the metacrisis. It is argued that much work under the heading of AI safety serves to perpetuate an unregulated space where Big AI can continue without meaningful change. Several suggestions for action at the level of the ACL are proposed. Finally, the logic of taking concerted action as a professional community is examined.

Event Factuality Prediction (EFP) is a cornerstone of robust Natural Language Understanding, aiming to determine the veridical status of events in text (Saurí and Pustejovsky, 2009). While approaches have evolved from rule-based systems (Saurí and Pustejovsky, 2012) to deep neural baselines trained on large-scale datasets (e.g., Stanovsky et al., 2017; Rudinger et al., 2018; Veyseh et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2022), the evaluation paradigm remains largely focused on treating factuality as a static classification task, i.e., assigning a fixed label (e.g., Factual, Counterfactual, or Uncertain) to an event.

Transformers (Vaswani et al., 2017) often focus attention on early positions in a manner largely insensitive to content. This attention sink has been observed in both small and large models (Xiao et al., 2024; Gu et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2024). It arises under various positional schemes—absolute/learned embeddings, ALiBi, RoPE, and even without explicit positional encodings (Press et al., 2021; Su et al., 2021; Gu et al., 2024)—and similar behavior appears in multimodal and vision settings, as well as in diffusion language models (Kang et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Feng and Sun, 2025; Rulli et al., 2025).

Transformers (Vaswani et al., 2017) routinely exhibit an attention sink: a persistent tendency to allocate disproportionate attention mass to early (often first) positions, independent of semantic content (Xiao et al., 2024; Gu et al., 2025). This effect has been observed across training stages and hyperparameters (Gu et al., 2025; Guo et al., 2024), across model families and datasets (Xiao et al., 2024), and under diverse positional encodings—including ALiBi (Press et al., 2022), RoPE (Su et al., 2023), and even no explicit positional encodings (Gu et al., 2025). Similar sink-like patterns have also been reported in large multimodal models and vision transformers (Kang et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Feng and Sun, 2025).

Large Language Models (LLMs) are pre-trained on massive data corpora, and the quality of these corpora is one of the main factors in achieving state-of-the-art performance. Standard pipelines typically include a series of heuristic filters (e.g., language identification, near-duplication detection, characters-to-other-signs ratio) aimed at improving downstream performance. An alternative or supplement to these filters is Classifier-based Quality Filtering (CQF), which offloads the filtering task to pre-trained models that provide quality scores. These scores are used not only to filter pre-training corpora but also to design curricula based on the scores. Nowadays, CQF is a cornerstone of many prominent datasets.

This work provides a unified critical analysis of group-based optimization methods. We propose a general formulation of GRPO-style methods, showing ten recent approaches as special cases. This perspective reveals shared issues, indicating that the surrogate objective is often dominated by weighting schemes, regularization, and importance sampling rather than pure reward maximization. Building on this formulation, we identify three recurring properties of GRPO-style training dynamics: (i) we analyze token-level gradients to demonstrate that non-uniform weighting induces systematic biases on shared prefix tokens; (ii) we study the interaction with AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017), showing that the training process remains invariant to global reward scaling across various scenarios; (iii) we show that optimizer momentum can drive policy updates beyond intended clipping boundaries during multi-step optimization. Beyond empirical performance, our analysis offers theoretical insights exposing a divergence between the surrogate objective and the true training goal. By characterizing these dynamics, our findings provide the community with a reference for the design and interpretation of LLM post-training strategies.

Persistent memory systems are essential for language model agents to maintain coherence in long-term interactions (Park et al., 2023). Beyond factual recall, long-horizon dialogue requires reasoning over temporal dependencies, causal chains, and multi-hop relationships across turns (Weller et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2025; Maharana et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2018). This necessitates memory representations that organize events into temporally grounded and relational structures (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019). Existing memory systems largely fall into two paradigms, flat memory and graph memory, exhibiting a trade-off between efficiency and structured reasoning, as illustrated in Figure 1.

3D visual grounding (3DVG) aims to localize target objects in a scene based on natural language descriptions. It is a fundamental capability for embodied AI, robotics, and human–scene interaction, where agents must reason jointly over language, visual appearance, and spatial structure.

Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong generative performance but remain prone to factual hallucinations, which hinder their reliable deployment. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) partially mitigates this issue by grounding model outputs in external knowledge (Lewis et al., 2020; Izacard et al., 2023; Mialon et al., 2023; Fan et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2025). More recently, agentic RAG systems extend this paradigm by introducing critic agents that evaluate model outputs and guide iterative actions over retrieval and generation (Asai et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Yan et al., 2024; Dong et al., 2025; Fang et al., 2026). In this work, we adopt the narrower definition of agentic RAG used in prior refinement-based systems, focusing on iterative correction over structured retrieval and generation operations rather than open-ended tool use or web-scale environments. Although critic-guided refinement can improve end-to-end performance, most approaches assume the critic is reliable and focus on using critic feedback for planning modules (Madaan et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Shinn et al., 2023), error taxonomies (Dong et al., 2025), and multi-step control flows (Asai et al., 2024; Zhou et al., 2024; Yan et al., 2024; Kim and Lee, 2024). In practice, LLM-based critics frequently misidentify failure causes and recommend ineffective corrections that can sometimes degrade performance relative to non-agentic baselines (Zheng et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2023; Kim and Lee, 2024). These observations suggest that reliance on explicit error categorization may introduce additional sources of uncertainty under noisy retrieval and generation.

The Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2023) underpins modern large language models (LLMs) (Brown et al., 2020; OpenAI et al., 2024; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025a), and as these models are deployed in agentic, real-world workloads, inference efficiency becomes a first-order concern (Aminabadi et al., 2022; Zhou et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2023). Agentic workloads require the model to handle very long contexts, maintain many persistent state items, and often produce long-form outputs (e.g., large codebases). As a result, they process on the order of 100× more tokens per inference than typical chatbot-style workloads (Wu et al., 2025). In this regime, caching and fast access to KV values shift the primary bottleneck from raw compute to memory capacity and memory bandwidth. That shift in turn changes the optimization landscape: permissible batch sizes shrink, GEMM inputs become “fat,” Tensor Core utilization drops, and available compute is severely underused.

While post-training techniques such as instruction tuning have successfully reduced many social biases in Large Language Models (LLMs), these systems remain vulnerable to cognitive biases inherited from human-generated data. A prominent example is the anchoring effect, in which quantitative judgments are disproportionately influenced by an irrelevant initial value. Existing work has demonstrated the presence of anchoring bias in LLMs and established that anchoring susceptibility varies substantially across model families and training paradigms. However, there is not yet a robust way of predicting when a model will be most susceptible to anchoring bias.

Relation extraction (RE) is a core NLP task that involves extracting [head, relation, dependent] RDF triples from text. In supervised settings, RE can be approached using various models, with graph-based parsers being one of the most popular paradigms. Although recent literature has explored the capacity of autoregressive LLMs to perform RE through in-context learning and supervision via causal language modeling, to the best of our knowledge, no direct comparison has yet been made between them and graph-based parsers in a supervised setting.

Despite rapid advances in AI with transformer-based LLMs (Vaswani et al., 2017; Brown et al., 2020; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024), most state-of-the-art systems remain static after training and lack the ability to learn continually during deployment. In many real-world settings, models need to adapt to new tasks, user preferences, or data distributions to perform optimally. While modern chatbots like ChatGPT achieve this by storing user memory (OpenAI, 2024) and using in-context learning (Brown et al., 2020) to incorporate this information, we currently lack solutions that can achieve this by modifying model weights during deployment. One reason this is challenging is that current post-training and adaptation methods for LLMs are exclusively gradient-based, including approaches such as SFT (Wei et al., 2022), RLHF (Ouyang et al., 2022), DPO (Rafailov et al., 2024), and GRPO (Shao et al., 2024). While effective, these methods require storing gradients, optimizer states, or intermediate activations, causing substantial memory overhead.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is central to aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with complex reasoning tasks (Jaech et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025). By leveraging outcome-based supervision, algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al., 2024) transform models from pattern matchers into rigorous reasoners (Yu et al., 2025a; Zheng et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2025; Liang et al., 2025a; Liu et al., 2025b; Zhao et al., 2025). However, the effectiveness of RL increasingly depends on data difficulty. High-quality reasoning datasets are scarce and rapidly absorbed into community training pipelines, leading to saturated benchmarks where strong base models already solve most instances (Liu et al., 2025a; Yang et al., 2025). This growing prevalence of saturated reasoning data fundamentally alters the learning dynamics of RL for LLMs.

Recent large language models (LLMs) achieve strong scores on mathematical benchmarks and can often generate proof-like text. However, their behavior frequently reflects pattern imitation rather than principled reasoning: models tend to reproduce familiar solution paths and can import a lemma’s conclusion without validating its hypotheses. Such behavior exploits surface correlations in the training distribution and undermines trustworthiness in mathematical reasoning.

As transformer model sizes continue to grow, the computational and energy demands of transformer inference have increased substantially. This has sparked significant interest in analog in-memory computing (AIMC) as a more energy-efficient alternative to traditional digital accelerators. Recent work in vision and speech has demonstrated that AIMC hardware can significantly improve energy efficiency and latency. However, state-of-the-art AIMC simulators primarily support CNN-based models and do not fully support transformer architectures.

Evaluation is central to progress in large language model (LLM) research. Increasingly, state-of-the-art systems are implemented as multistage pipelines rather than single-model predictors, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-using agents, prompt chains, and planner–executor architectures. In these systems, reported evaluation outcomes depend not only on the underlying model but also on intermediate components and configuration choices. Reproducing LLM pipeline evaluations therefore requires access to evaluation-specific artifacts such as generation and evaluation prompts, judge model configurations, retrieval corpus snapshots, tool schemas, and intermediate execution traces. While some artifacts may be released via code or supplementary material, their availability and completeness are inconsistent across papers, leaving the reproducibility and independent validation of published evaluations unclear. Prior work has proposed general reproducibility checklists and artifact evaluation processes, primarily focused on model training, datasets, and code release. More recently, standardized formats for evaluation reporting have been proposed to improve transparency. However, these approaches do not explicitly target the reproducibility requirements of evaluation execution in multi-stage LLM pipelines, nor do they empirically assess whether the necessary artifacts are reported in current practice.

Reasoning has become a central goal in Large Language Model (LLM) development (Xu et al. , 2025), with models now designed to produce step-by-step traces before responding (Zelikman et al. , 2022). By scaling compute at test time, these models can assist with complex, multi-step tasks such as Deep Research (Shao et al. , 2024), software assistance (Wang et al. , 2024), and scientific automation (Lu et al. , 2024). Offline evaluations ensure such models behave as intended (Baker et al. , 2025). A common format is multiple-choice question answering (Clark et al. , 2020, MCQA): from a set of choices, select the best answer to a question. While popular, research shows that non-reasoning LLMs outperform random guessing in MCQA even without the question (Balepur et al. , 2024b), i.e.,.

The interpretation of medical imaging, particularly three-dimensional (3D) volumetric data such as chest Computed Tomography (CT), remains a cornerstone of modern diagnostic medicine. Despite its importance, generating radiology reports that are accurate, comprehensive, and clinically valid remains cognitively demanding and represents a primary bottleneck in clinical workflows. While Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models have shown promise in automating radiology report generation, these approaches often exhibit clinical hallucinations, struggle to detect subtle pathological findings in sparse 3D data, and lack iterative verification and cross-checking.

Parsing a string with respect to a context-free grammar (CFG) involves determining whether—and with what weight—the grammar generates that string. Prefix parsing addresses the related question of whether an input prefix can be extended to a complete string generated by the grammar. In the probabilistic setting, these tasks correspond to computing (i) the probability that the grammar generates a given string, and (ii) the total probability of strings beginning with a given prefix. Existing prefix parsers are typically tied to specific parsing algorithms.
Prosody broadly refers to aspects of speech that complement lexical content, conveying intent-related or paralinguistic information.

Language models (LMs) are pre-trained using causal language modeling (CLM), a next-token prediction objective (Radford et al., 2018). While CLM pre-training equips LMs with world knowledge and general capabilities (Brown et al., 2020; Kojima et al., 2022), it does not optimize for linguistic competence, i.e., the capacity to comprehend and interpret diverse linguistic phenomena (Chomsky, 1965; Waldis et al., 2024). Consequently, LMs often behave as stochastic parrots (Bender et al., 2021), mimicking surface-level patterns without grasping the underlying linguistic scaffolding (Chang and Bergen, 2024; López-Otal et al., 2025). This phenomenon mirrors rote learning in humans (Plunkett and Marchman, 1993), where learners reproduce patterns without understanding the generative rules (Brown and Berko, 1960; Myles et al., 1998). We hypothesize that pre-training on language learning tasks, which require processing beyond raw sequence reconstruction, can stimulate the development of linguistic competence. Specifically, we target data-efficient acquisition of morphological, syntactic, and semantic knowledge. Inspired by human language acquisition, this approach encourages the development of structured representations that go beyond surface-level co-occurrence (Alishahi, 2011; Perfors et al., 2011; Culbertson and Adger, 2014). Evidence suggests that both humans and neural networks benefit from structured linguistic input during learning (Elman, 1993; Galke et al., 2024; Hu et al., 2025).

Multilingual pre-trained models have significantly advanced machine translation for low-resource languages through cross-lingual transfer learning. However, performance across extremely low-resource settings exhibits a staggering degree of variation. Recent studies show that while some African and ancient languages can achieve BLEU scores exceeding 40, certain American or South Asian indigenous languages struggle to reach 5 BLEU under similar conditions. This disparity creates a significant barrier for the MT community. Without a standardized way to provide context for these results, it is difficult to interpret whether a high BLEU score indicates an effective model or a benchmark with unnaturally low complexity.

Large language models (LLMs) have become indispensable tools for knowledge-intensive tasks, ranging from summarizing medical records and drafting clinical notes to screening legal contracts and detecting anomalous financial transactions. As these models are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare and finance, privacy has emerged as a critical requirement for their responsible use. Consequently, recent security research has revisited a threat model long studied for classifiers and regressors: membership inference attacks.

Cybergrooming involves the sexual exploitation of minors by adults in digital environments (Wachs et al., 2012). It is an escalating social issue that causes severe psychological and potential physical harm to vulnerable minors (Schittenhelm et al., 2025). Automated cybergrooming detection systems (Inches and Crestani, 2012) can help protect young users on digital platforms, but their development is constrained by data scarcity and legal restrictions, limiting access to sufficient suitable training data for building accurate detection models (An et al., 2025a).

Large language models (LLMs) undergo extensive alignment training to instill human-defined safety policies, mitigating risks associated with misuse, bias, and harmful outputs (Kenton et al., 2021; Matthews et al., 2022). These models are aligned across various responsible AI (RAI) concepts to refuse harmful prompts and promote safe deployment. However, the notion of what is harmful varies across contexts (He et al., 2024; Yuan et al., 2025); for example, providing medical advice may be harmful in some situations (Wang et al., 2024) but essential in others, such as in medical chatbots (Xie et al., 2024). This contextual variability makes fixed alignment configurations insufficient for many real-world deployments (Yuan et al., 2025). While retraining models for each use case is one option, it incurs substantial computational and developmental costs. To address this challenge, we investigate the effects of narrow, targeted interventions on already aligned models as an efficient alternative.

Vision–language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed to generate textual descriptions of visual content. A central challenge in generating such descriptions is determining the appropriate level of specificity: which information should be included and at what level of detail? While specificity is crucial for communicative effectiveness, it is notoriously difficult to measure. A common practice is to treat description length as a proxy for specificity, assuming the description is accurate and well-formed. However, the relationship between length and specificity is not straightforward; descriptions can be lengthy yet vacuous, or concise yet rich in detail. This paper constructs a dataset that manipulates length independently of information content, pairing images with descriptions that are either lengthy yet verbose or concise yet information-dense. We operationalize specificity through contrastive image compatibility: a description is more specific to the extent that it identifies the target image from a large set of alternatives. Using this framework, we demonstrate that human preferences track specificity rather than length, and we examine how different specificity constraints in prompts affect the specificity of VLM-generated descriptions. Our key finding is that controlling for length alone cannot account for differences in specificity; it is how the length budget is applied that matters. These results support evaluation approaches that directly measure specificity rather than relying on length as a proxy.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are trained on vast collections of textual data, which may inadvertently contain sensitive personal information or copyrighted content. To address this issue, recent studies have explored LLM unlearning—a post-hoc approach that aims to remove a model’s memorized or internally encoded representations of specific private or copyrighted content without retraining the model from scratch. Early unlearning methods typically designate the entire text sequence in a given forget dataset as the unlearning target. However, this approach often results in over-forgetting, where unnecessary knowledge deletion leads to a noticeable degradation in overall model performance and utility. More recent work instead focuses on selectively identifying token-level or span-level unlearning targets within a text. While this line of work has demonstrated improved preservation of model utility, the identification of unlearning targets commonly depends on signals provided by external models.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into clinical workflows, from patient-facing communication to decision support (Rajpurkar et al., 2022; Artsi et al., 2025). However, high benchmark accuracy alone does not ensure safe deployment. In practice, clinical systems often rely on a model’s confidence score to triage cases, trigger escalation, or defer to clinicians (Dvijotham et al., 2023). Therefore, reliability becomes a first-class requirement: models must be accurate and well-calibrated, so that higher confidence corresponds to a higher likelihood of correctness, and their confidence signals should remain stable under benign input variations (Kuzucu et al., 2024). Healthcare further amplifies these concerns: if sensitive identity cues systematically affect clinical decisions or uncertainty estimates, they risk inequitable and unsafe patient care (Zack et al., 2024).

Abductive reasoning (Peirce, 1931; Frankfurt, 1958) is a cornerstone of human intelligence, denoting the inference process toward the best explanatory hypothesis from observation. This ability is fundamental to complex cognitive tasks ranging from commonsense reasoning to scientific discovery (Bhagavatula et al., 2020; Bisk et al., 2019). Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) (Liu et al., 2023; Google, 2025) have shown remarkable progress in perception-grounded reasoning tasks. However, the extent to which these models can perform abductive reasoning remains unclear. Prior benchmarks such as VAR (Liang et al., 2022) and Sherlock (Hessel et al., 2022) are limited to static, single-agent inference with fixed candidate sets, leaving open the question of how VLMs behave when abductive reasoning must be both generated and evaluated in dynamic, multiagent scenarios.

Event relations capture structured semantic dependencies between events, such as causal, temporal, and sub-event relations. In natural language, such relations are often expressed implicitly across sentences. For example, when a narrative mentions a power outage and a train delay, a meaningful relation can be inferred from context without explicit connectives. In the era of large language models (LLMs), understanding event relations goes beyond recognizing isolated events and is crucial for higher-level reasoning and coherent, temporally and causally grounded generation. Existing studies on event relation extraction have primarily focused on improving model performance, ranging from fine-tuning LLMs to instruction-based alignment, as well as single-agent and multi-agent approaches. In terms of interpretability, prior work has examined the explainability of event detection or leveraged event knowledge to generate explanatory analyses. While these studies provide useful insights into how event information supports interpretability, comparatively little attention has been paid to interpreting event relations themselves, particularly at the level of internal model representations.

Coreference resolution remains a challenging task in natural language processing, as it depends on decisions that transcend sentence boundaries and require full discourse context and world knowledge. Despite considerable progress, most research still focuses predominantly on English. Additionally, fictional texts present further challenges not covered by standard benchmark datasets, such as long documents and a high proportion of pronouns and dialogue. The type and length of texts in commonly used datasets are predominantly short news texts or older literature. Therefore, new data resources and models are needed for cultural analytics.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance, yet their English-centric development limits their effectiveness for non-English users (Hadi et al., 2024, 2023). Recent efforts (Xue et al., 2021; Workshop et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2023) aim to enhance multilingual capabilities, though English-centric models still underperform in low-resource languages (Qin et al., 2024; OpenAI et al., 2024). A key issue is language confusion (Devine, 2024), where models fail to consistently generate the desired language, particularly in non-English contexts (Marchisio et al., 2024). Techniques to mitigate this include temperature lowering, few-shot prompting, and fine-tuning (Marchisio et al., 2024), but these come with limitations such as reduced response diversity (Agarwal et al., 2024; Renze and Guven, 2024) or increased computational costs.

Humor is a uniquely human trait, and its interpretation involves language and social understanding, creativity, and common-sense reasoning (Brock, 2017; Martin and Ford, 2018; Attardo, 2020), making it an attractive challenge for Computational Linguistics. Prior work has explored a range of humor-related tasks, including humor detection (Taylor and Mazlack, 2004; Mihalcea and Strapparava, 2006), generation (Hessel et al., 2023), and even editing (Horvitz et al., 2024). However, most available humor datasets focus on familiar forms such as satirical headlines, puns, or short one-liners, leaving other varieties underexplored. In this paper, we introduce a novel dataset for an understudied form of textual humor—intentionally bad humor—through sentences drawn from the Bulwer-Lytton Fiction Contest 1 (BLFC).

Large language models (LLMs) now incorporate sophisticated long-term memory that persists across conversations (Fountas et al., 2024; Zhong et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023), while demonstrating remarkable emotional capabilities that can surpass human performance on standardized tests by over 40% (Schlegel et al., 2025). These systems promise to remember our preferences, understand our context, and respond with finely-tuned emotional intelligence (Li et al., 2023). Yet this convergence of personalization and emotional intelligence reveals a troubling reality: user memory systematically shapes LLMs’ emotional judgments, with identical scenarios producing markedly different interpretations based on user profiles. Multiple high-performing models exhibit larger shifts in emotional understanding for users with disadvantaged profiles, along with systematic demographic biases across gender, religion, and age (Table 1, Figure 3, 4), suggesting that personalization may be internalizing social hierarchies directly into the models’ reasoning processes. To mitigate these disparities, we curate a general-purpose preference dataset designed to reduce the influence of demographic profiles on emotional reasoning.

As human-agent interaction evolves from transactional assistants to long-term social companions, users demand agents that maintain a personalized, consistent Original Character (OC) persona over time. Such companions must proactively manage shared memories, track evolving preferences, and sustain suspension of disbelief over long-horizon interactions. Yet, current large language model (LLM)-based agents, primarily optimized by prompt engineering or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), face a critical generalization gap in these settings. While existing methods perform well on multi-turn dialogue benchmarks, they still struggle in long-horizon, socially rich interactions.

Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), particularly in complex mathematical and coding tasks. Despite its demonstrated effectiveness, GRPO faces a critical limitation in properly balancing between exploitation and exploration during policy optimization, which can undermine its performance. Excessive exploitation can cause the model to become overconfident in its suboptimal solutions, thereby limiting its ability to explore novel reasoning strategies and potentially overlooking more effective approaches. Conversely, while exploration is necessary for identifying better policies, excessive exploration may result in unstable training dynamics and hinder convergence to a stable, high-performing solution. These opposing risks highlight the importance of a principled mechanism for balancing exploration and exploitation to achieve a more robust GRPO.

Training a large language model (LLM) is a costly and challenging process, which can be divided into three phases: pretraining, where the model is trained on a large corpus of text; supervised fine-tuning (SFT), where the model is trained on selected input/output pairs to learn tasks such as following instructions; and preference learning, which includes various additional learning steps like reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR).

Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) (Edge et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2024) extends large language models (LLMs) with structured knowledge graphs (KGs), enabling graph-aware context selection and more coherent multi-hop reasoning over external knowledge sources (Peng et al., 2024; Han et al., 2025; Saleh et al., 2024). However, recent work has revealed that the graph construction and retrieval mechanisms that make GraphRAG effective also introduce a new and under-explored attack surface. In particular, knowledge poisoning attacks can inject spurious entities and relationships into the corpus used to build the knowledge graph, thereby corrupting the retrieved query-specific subgraph and steering the generator toward incorrect answers (Liang et al., 2025; Wen et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2025). Despite the severity of this threat, GraphRAG-specific defenses remain limited. Prior mitigations such as query paraphrasing (Zou et al., 2025), LLM-based knowledge referencing (Liang et al., 2025), and poisoning-text identification (Jain et al., 2023) operate at the query or passage level and therefore fail to address the structural nature of GraphRAG poisoning (Appendix A).

Natural-language (NL) interfaces to databases enable enterprise analytics for non-coding experts by translating NL questions into executable SQL queries (Zelle and Mooney, 1996; Yu et al., 2018). While prior text-to-SQL work has demonstrated strong performance on simpler academic benchmarks like SPIDER (Yu et al., 2018) and BIRD (Li et al., 2023), these often fail to capture the full complexity of real-world applications. To evaluate text-to-SQL in more realistic settings, Lei et al. (2025) introduced Spider 2.0, which presents significant challenges such as large cross-domain databases, nested data types, and long, complex SQL queries.

While large language models (LLMs) can be deployed in scientific workflows—from literature reviews to hypothesis generation and experimental planning—their capacity to perform fundamental scientific tasks remains poorly understood. Scientific feasibility assessment determines whether a claim aligns with established knowledge and whether concrete experiments could support or refute it. Feasibility assessment requires diagnostic reasoning about experimental designs, expected outcomes, and evidential alignment.

Large-scale annotations of subjective, discourse-dependent social interactions remain a critical bottleneck in computational social science (Zimba and Gasparyan, 2021). Human expert annotations are inefficient, and crowdwork is costly and difficult to standardize for nuanced constructs (Mikulová et al., 2022; Horych et al., 2025). Researchers increasingly turn to LLMs for automated annotations, given their human-level performance in some settings (Tseng et al., 2025). When annotating millions of social media chats, posts, and comments under tight constraints, existing LLM pipelines face a persistent quality–deployability trade-off, as high-performing pipelines typically involve prohibitive cost and latency (Zhou et al., 2024), while efficiency-oriented ones tend to lose the contextual nuance needed for subtle interpretations (Lu et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2024). As a result, researchers are often forced to choose between unaffordable accuracy and scalable, shallow annotation.

The faithfulness of the reasoning process in large language models (LLMs) has become a central concern in recent studies. This concern is particularly salient when model-generated text is interpreted as an explanation of the model’s internal reasoning process. For instance, the faithfulness of chain-of-thought (CoT) has been widely questioned. Lanham et al. (2023) and Barez et al. (2025) find that LLMs can produce correct answers even when the generated CoT is incorrect. Lyu et al. (2023) observe that answer information is implicitly encoded in features of intermediate layers even before CoT generation. However, this paper focuses on a more typical issue: LLMs may incorporate incorrect connotations into irrelevant phrases and use these to bias language generation. Specifically, when preceding tokens do not provide informative evidence for the answer, they may not only serve basic syntactic functions but also bias the LLM toward the target answer.

Non-autoregressive (NAR) text generation has emerged as a promising direction for accelerating language models through fully parallel token processing. Recent diffusion-based approaches have narrowed the gap between the output text quality of NAR and classic autoregressive models. Despite some advances, diffusion-style models still require numerous iterative denoising steps to numerically solve the underlying stochastic differential equation, which defines a continuous trajectory in latent space along which noise is gradually transformed into data. A high number of steps often eliminates the computational gain from predicting all tokens in parallel.

The prevailing post-training paradigm for Large Language Models (LLMs) typically involves Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) followed by Reinforcement Learning (RL). SFT primarily serves to align models with human instructions and enhance specialized capabilities cost-effectively. Mainstream research in SFT has focused on data engineering. However, the standard Cross-Entropy (CE) loss mechanism, which pushes probability mass toward the target label, implicitly suppresses diversity. This reduction in generation diversity severely constrains the model’s exploration space during the subsequent RL phase. To mitigate mode collapse, existing studies have proposed extending beyond pure CE loss by modifying the update policy or incorporating diversity regularization terms. However, their application is often restricted to the RL stage, or the performance trade-offs incurred during the SFT phase may not be fully recovered in subsequent RL steps.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are highly fluent but can be brittle when meaning depends on event structure, participant roles, or lexical ambiguity. Frame Semantics addresses this by modeling situations as frames evoked by lexical units, with typed participant roles and relations capturing abstraction, causality, temporal structure, and perspective. Injecting FrameNet knowledge into LLMs can strengthen event-level representations and support inference beyond surface-level lexical overlap. Recent work has begun to explore the interaction between LLMs and frame-semantic knowledge, providing initial evidence that injecting FrameNet supervision into Llama via LoRA can improve frame-semantic role labeling. Related studies suggest that LLMs can implicitly encode frame knowledge and perform frame identification reasonably well. Beyond frame identification, prior work has used Frame Semantics to induce structured knowledge by clustering shared event structures and participant roles. Other studies further suggest that event and relational knowledge in LLMs is often latent but remains incomplete without explicit supervision.

Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across multiple clients without sharing raw data, thereby preserving privacy in domains such as healthcare. However, FL does not eliminate the risk of memorization, where large language models (LLMs) may inadvertently encode sensitive data.

Figurative language—such as metaphor, metonymy, and simile—serves as a powerful tool for expressing abstract meanings. While crucial for language understanding, detecting these figures is complicated by their shared semantic deviation from literal meaning despite distinct cognitive drivers. Despite significant progress in figurative language detection, two fundamental gaps persist. First, existing approaches are overwhelmingly framed as single-category binary classifiers; even multi-task extensions target broad comprehension tasks (e.g., NLI) rather than the fine-grained disambiguation of cognitively related figures. Second, no unified framework has been proposed to jointly resolve the inherent ambiguity among the confusable trio of metaphor, metonymy, and simile.

The development of Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems continues to face a fundamental challenge: many languages remain underrepresented due to the limited availability of annotated corpora and reliable evaluation benchmarks. This issue is particularly evident in linguistically rich regions such as India, where numerous languages with millions of speakers are still inadequately supported. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising approach to bridging this gap by enabling knowledge transfer from high-resource to low-resource languages through cross-lingual pretraining and generation.

Recent advances in neural network technology have enabled high-fidelity text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis models. These models typically convert input text into a phoneme sequence using a grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) converter, followed by generative models that produce speech from the phoneme sequence. However, G2P is generally based on morphological analysis and may fail to generate correct pronunciations in ambiguous languages like Japanese, where word readings and meanings can vary depending on context.

Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-stage pipelines, where visual inputs are processed or reconstructed before being consumed by language models. A common instance of this paradigm is image inpainting, in which missing or corrupted regions are filled prior to downstream generative tasks. Although modern diffusion-based inpainting models produce visually plausible reconstructions, they are optimized primarily for pixel-level realism, allowing subtle but semantically meaningful artifacts to be introduced without being perceptually salient. Despite visually coherent reconstructions, localized inpainting artifacts lead to object substitutions, attribute changes, or category-level errors in downstream captions. Because captioning models lack explicit awareness of which regions have been reconstructed, synthesized content may be treated as genuine visual evidence. This raises a central question: to what extent does reconstruction fidelity influence downstream caption correctness and semantic grounding? Despite the widespread use of inpainting and captioning, this relationship remains underexplored.

Commonsense reasoning is central to human cognition and a long-standing challenge in artificial intelligence and natural language understanding. Developmental studies suggest that for humans, it emerges from intuitive, experience-based frameworks in early childhood and becomes more abstract and socially grounded through embodied experience, social interaction, cultural transmission, and language. In contrast, large language models acquire “commonsense-like” knowledge indirectly from large-scale text corpora via objectives such as next-token prediction, rather than through grounded interaction or social learning. Despite this, LLMs exhibit emergent behaviors resembling human intuitive reasoning, including inferring intentions and anticipating plausible actions. However, this competence is brittle, as models fail under minimal semantic perturbations, struggle with logical consistency, and rely on statistical shortcuts rather than genuine reasoning. To improve the evaluation of commonsense reasoning, we introduce LOGICAL-COMMONSENSEQA, a benchmark that reframes the task as a logical composition over multiple plausible answers, requiring models to reason about relationships between plausible statements rather than select a single response.

Dense retrievers learn vector representations of text from large-scale unsupervised, supervised, and synthetic corpora, achieving strong performance on general-domain information retrieval (IR) benchmarks. However, these models often fail to capture biomedical-specific semantics, limiting their effectiveness in tasks involving specialized terminology. To bridge this gap, various biomedical IR models have been proposed. Encoder-based biomedical language models, such as BiomedBERT, pretrain transformer encoders on large-scale biomedical corpora to capture domain-specific terminology and semantics, but their retrieval effectiveness is limited by the availability of retrieval task-specific supervision. More recently, large-scale biomedical IR models, including MedCPT and BMRetriever, leverage contrastive learning on extensive biomedical semantic-related text pairs to achieve improved semantic alignment. Despite their effectiveness, these models depend on computationally expensive training and coarse-grained relevance signals.

Despite significant advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) for code intelligence tasks such as code generation and completion, repository-level code completion remains a challenging area. Traditional code completion relies solely on in-file context from the partially written code. In contrast, real-world development often requires external knowledge spread across other files within the same repository—referred to as cross-file context. However, due to the limited context length of LLMs, it is infeasible to provide entire repositories as input. Instead, retrieval mechanisms must supply only the most relevant code fragments to the model.

Retrospective forecasting (RF) evaluates forecasting systems on questions whose outcomes are already known. This setup requires that evidence available to the forecaster predates the resolution of each question. Without this guarantee, post-resolution information can leak into the retrieved documents, artificially inflating accuracy and undermining the validity of the evaluation. Forecasting future events is a critical task for decision-making in policy, business, and science. Recent work has explored whether large language models (LLMs) can match or exceed human forecasters. Unlike most NLP tasks where static test sets suffice, evaluating forecasting ability poses a distinct challenge: ground-truth labels are only observed once future events resolve, which may take months or years. RF sidesteps this delay by backtesting on resolved questions while enforcing an information cutoff that restricts evidence to what was available at the time of prediction. This enables rapid iteration and immediate quantitative feedback. In practice, most RF pipelines enforce the cutoff using search-engine date filters or by filtering on reported publication timestamps.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multilingual settings, yet our understanding of their internal reasoning remains heavily skewed toward English. While recent work suggests that LLMs may internally “think” in English or exhibit an English-centric representational topology, less is known about whether higher-level meta-cognitive attributes generalize across languages.

Listwise reranking has emerged as a powerful paradigm in modern information retrieval, leveraging Large Language Models to evaluate candidate documents simultaneously rather than in isolation. By integrating the query and the full document list within a single prompt, this approach enables the model to capture global inter-document dependencies, delivering ranking performance that substantially outperforms traditional pointwise or pairwise methods. However, this paradigm faces a fundamental theoretical flaw: the violation of Permutation Invariance. Theoretically, an ideal ranking function must yield results that are invariant to the physical sequence of candidate documents. In practice, however, LLMs exhibit intrinsic sensitivity to token positions, inevitably giving rise to severe position bias. This often manifests as the “Lost in the Middle” phenomenon, where models systematically favor documents at the beginning or end of the context while overlooking highly relevant ones in the middle, thereby degrading the overall reliability of the retrieval system.

The rapid advancement of AI has dramatically accelerated scientific progress, producing thousands of new publications each year. However, reproducing these results remains a major bottleneck: many papers omit critical implementation details, code repositories are incomplete or unavailable, and essential background knowledge is scattered across diverse sources. While humans perform the tedious pipeline of reading papers, inspecting code, and collecting background materials to reproduce results, enabling machines to perform the same workflow reliably remains an open challenge.

The emergence of “System 2” Multimodal Reasoning Models (MRMs), which are post-trained via SFT and RL to generate step-by-step reasoning, has driven remarkable progress in mathematical and logical domains. By leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL) (Lambert et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2025) and long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) (Wei et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022) inference, MRMs demonstrate the ability to self-correct and reason through complex problems. Separately, CoT prompting is a general technique that instructs any Multimodal Language Model (MLM) to think step-by-step before answering. However, a fundamental question remains: does this text-centric reasoning paradigm translate to spatial intelligence? Spatial reasoning requires grounding, geometric intuition, and precise localization, which are skills that may not easily arise from verbose, text-based reasoning (Tong et al., 2024a, b).

Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in Information Extraction, traditionally addressed via sequence labeling (Devlin et al., 2019) or span classification (Sohrab and Miwa, 2018). Recently, generative approaches have gained traction, utilizing Sequence-to-Sequence models (Yan et al., 2021) or Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate entity sequences directly. Among these, DiffusionNER (Shen et al., 2023) proposed a novel paradigm by modeling NER as a boundary diffusion process. By treating entity spans as continuous coordinates generated from a Gaussian distribution, diffusion models offer the theoretical advantage of iteratively refining predictions, capturing complex inter-entity dependencies through a multi-step denoising process.

Proteins are the fundamental building blocks of life, governing a complex network of interconnected functional mechanisms within an organism (Levitt, 2009). Since their biological functions and 3D structures are primarily encoded in their amino acid sequences—effectively the “language of life” (Heinzinger et al., 2019)—a vast amount of research has been conducted to develop sequence-based protein representation learners (Ibtehaz and Kihara, 2023). This trend has been further inspired by the success of Natural Language Processing, particularly through unsupervised masked language modeling (Devlin et al., 2019), which has enabled the learning of robust protein representations suitable for various applications (Meier et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2023).

本文揭示了基于分类器的质量过滤模型中存在的严重缺陷。我们证明，对文档进行简单的维基百科风格格式化即可系统性地绕过过滤阈值，从而使本应被拒绝的内容得以进入预训练语料库。此外，我们还发现这一现象在不同领域均普遍存在，同时证实了先前的研究结论，即CQF模型在质量评估方面存在领域依赖性偏差。我们的研究结果表明，CQF教师模型所给出的“教育类”质量评分可能被高估，从而对数据的实际价值做出过于乐观的判断。

本文对基于群体的优化方法进行了统一的批判性分析。我们提出了GRPO类方法的通用形式，并将十种近期提出的方法作为其特例。这一视角揭示了这些方法共有的问题：代理目标往往受权重方案、正则化项及重要性采样所主导，而非单纯由奖励最大化决定。基于这一形式化描述，我们识别出GRPO类训练动态中的三个反复出现的特性：（i）通过分析词元级梯度，我们证明非均匀权重会导致共享前缀词元出现系统性偏差；（ii）我们研究了与AdamW优化器的相互作用，发现训练过程在各种场景下对全局奖励缩放具有不变性；（iii）我们证明，在多步优化过程中，优化器的动量会使策略更新超出预期的截断边界。除了实证性能外，我们的分析还提供了理论见解，揭示了代理目标与真实训练目标之间的差异。通过对这些动态进行刻画，我们的研究结果为LLM后训练策略的设计与解释提供了参考依据。

持久化记忆系统对于语言模型代理在长期交互中保持连贯性至关重要（Park等人，2023）。除了事实性记忆外，长时程对话还需要对时间依赖关系、因果链条以及跨轮次的多跳关系进行推理（Weller等人，2025；Huang等人，2025；Maharana等人，2024；Wu等人，2024；Yang等人，2018）。这要求记忆系统能够将事件组织成具有时间基础且相互关联的结构（Kwiatkowski等人，2019）。现有的记忆系统主要分为扁平化记忆与图结构记忆两种范式，如图1所示，二者在效率与结构化推理能力之间存在权衡。
3D视觉定位（3DVG）旨在根据自然语言描述来定位场景中的目标物体。这是具身人工智能、机器人技术以及人机场景交互中的基本能力，因为智能体需要同时处理语言、视觉外观以及空间结构信息。

关系抽取（RE）是一项核心的自然语言处理任务，其目标是从文本中提取[头实体、关系、尾实体]形式的RDF三元组（Candan等人，2001；Zhao等人，2024）。在监督学习设置下，RE任务可采用多种模型来解决，其中基于图的解析器是最流行的范式之一（Verga等人，2018；Tang等人，2022）。尽管近期已有研究探讨了自回归大语言模型通过上下文学习来执行RE任务的能力（Wan等人，2023；Bi等人，2024；Wei等人，2024），以及通过因果语言建模进行监督的方法（Zhang等人，2024；Papaluca等人，2024；Gajo和Barrón-Cedeño，2025），但据我们所知，目前尚未有研究在监督学习设置下对这些方法与基于图的解析器进行直接比较。
尽管基于Transformer的LLM（Vaswani等人，2017；Brown等人，2020；DeepSeek-AI等人，2024）取得了快速进展，但大多数最先进的系统在训练完成后仍保持静态，缺乏在部署过程中持续学习的能力。在许多实际应用场景中，模型需要适应新任务、用户偏好或数据分布，才能实现最佳性能。

本文提出了一种训练框架RULES（通过资格推理与分段感知强化学习实现引理的可靠使用）。该框架基于分组相对策略优化（GRPO）（Shao等人，2024），并采用分段感知损失掩码机制——该机制会对导致错误的特定分段施加惩罚，而非对整个输出序列进行惩罚。这种设计使得监督信号与任务所需的认知分解方式相一致，促使模型学会“先检查后使用”的原则，而非过度拟合标签层面的捷径。

本研究利用硬件感知模拟技术表明，模拟噪声会导致性能下降，这种下降具有持续性，且受任务类型与模型架构的影响；其对需要复杂推理的任务影响更为显著，而对句子级分类任务的影响则较小。子模块与注意力层面的分析显示，Q/K/V投影层以及早期的注意力生成机制最为脆弱，而前馈层则相对稳健。此外，模拟推理并非均匀失效，而是会破坏那些负责构建注意力结构与上下文推理的内部机制。这些发现为设计更稳健的模拟变压器提供了实用指导，也推动了未来关于硬件感知注意力稳定性的研究。

本文提出了一种将前缀解析转化为普通解析的通用方法，使得其他解析器也能适用于前缀解析场景。该方法基于前缀文法——一种仅比原文法大一个常数倍的新文法，能够精确生成原文法的加权前缀语言。因此，任何解析算法均可直接作为前缀解析器使用：其输入长度依赖性保持不变，而额外开销仅来自文法结构因素。此外，通过算法微分技术，我们提出了计算下一个token权重向量的最快已知算法。
韵律泛指那些能够补充词汇内容、传达意图相关或副语言信息的语音特征。例如，音高与能量的局部变化、停顿以及时长延长等，均可用于表达信息重点、讽刺语气、自我修正，或是陈述句与疑问句之间的区别。更宽的音高范围及更快的语速则能传达兴奋情绪。在向量空间模型中，无论是显式还是隐式地表示韵律信息，对于语音生成与理解都至关重要。

大型语言模型（LLMs）经过广泛的对齐训练，以植入人类定义的安全策略，从而降低因滥用、偏见及有害输出所带来的风险（Kenton等人）。这些模型在多种负责任的AI（RAI）概念上进行了对齐，以便拒绝有害的提示并促进安全部署。然而，何为有害在不同情境下存在差异（He等人）。例如，在某些情况下提供医疗建议可能是有害的（Wang等人），但在其他情况下则至关重要，如医疗聊天机器人中（Xie等人）。这种情境上的差异性使得固定的对齐配置难以满足许多实际应用场景的需求（Yuan等人）。虽然为每种使用场景重新训练模型是一种选择，但这会带来巨大的计算和开发成本。为解决这一挑战，我们研究了针对已对齐模型实施有限且精准的干预措施的效果，作为一种更高效的替代方案。
为生成信息丰富的回答，检索准确的候选项至关重要；否则，后续阶段可能会受到负面影响，从而导致输出结果不连贯。

本文构建了一个数据集，该数据集能够独立于信息内容来调整描述的长度，将图像与那些冗长却空洞（啰嗦）或简洁却信息丰富（复合型）的描述配对。我们利用对比图像兼容性来量化特异性：描述的特异性取决于其从大量备选图像中准确识别出目标图像的能力。基于这一框架，我们发现人类的偏好更关注特异性而非长度，并分析了提示中不同的特异性约束（如要求简洁或设定字符限制）如何影响视觉语言模型生成的描述的特异性。我们的核心发现是，仅控制长度无法解释特异性差异；关键在于如何分配长度预算。这些结果支持那些直接测量特异性而非依赖长度作为代理指标的评估方法。
大型语言模型（LLMs）是在海量的文本数据上训练的，这些数据中可能无意中包含敏感的个人隐私信息或受版权保护的内容。为解决这一问题，近期研究提出了LLM遗忘技术，这是一种事后处理方法，旨在在不重新训练模型的情况下，消除模型对特定隐私或受版权保护内容的记忆或内部编码表示（Zhang等人）。
大型语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地融入临床工作流程中，从与患者的沟通到决策支持（Rajpurkar等人）。
归纳推理（Peirce, 1931; Frankfurt, 1958）是人类智能的核心要素，指的是从观察中推导出最佳解释性假设的推理过程。
本文提出了UERLens，一种用于分析大型语言模型中事件关系可解释性的框架。该框架包含三个主要组成部分：首先，我们构建了一个涵盖因果、时间以及子事件关系这三种基本事件关系类型的大规模反事实数据集，以便对特定关系的影响进行受控分析；其次，我们采用稀疏自编码器来分解模型的中间激活状态，从而识别出与特定事件关系密切相关的内部特征；最后，我们通过模型干预和训练等手段，探究这些关系敏感特征的功能作用。

大型语言模型（LLMs）的推理过程是否可靠，已成为近期研究中的核心问题（Wei等人，2022；Kojima等人，2022；Wang等人，2023a）。当模型生成的文本被用作解释其内部推理过程时，这一问题尤为突出。例如，在思维链（CoT）方面，其可靠性已受到广泛质疑。Lanham等人（2023）和Barez等人（2025）的研究发现，即使生成的CoT存在错误，LLMs仍可能得出正确答案。Lyu等人（2023）则发现，在生成CoT之前，答案的信息就已经通过中间层的特征被隐含地编码了。然而，本文关注的是LLMs推理过程中更为典型的问题，即LLMs可能会将错误的含义赋予那些与问题无关的词语，并利用这些错误含义来影响语言生成。

GPT-2 में ध्यान के “सिंक” के पीछे का सर्किट: सीखी गई क्वेरी पूर्वाग्रह (bQ), पहली परत के MLP द्वारा स्थानिक एन्कोडिंग का रूपांतरण, एवं की प्रोजेक्शन में निर्देशांक स्तर की संरचना (Wk)।
क्लासिफायर-आधारित गुणवत्ता फिल्टरिंग मॉडलों में एक महत्वपूर्ण कमजोरी है।
यह कार्य समूह-आधारित अनुकूलन विधियों पर एक एकीकृत आलोचनात्मक विश्लेषण प्रस्तुत करता है।
यह कार्य, उपयोगकर्ता की प्राथमिकताओं को संग्रहीत करने से पहले पूर्व-तर्क द्वारा अनुमान की जिम्मेदारी को याददाश्त चरण में स्थानांतरित करके, दीर्घकालिक व्यक्तिगत स्थिरता को लक्ष्य रखता है।

3D विजुअल ग्राउंडिंग (3DVG) प्राकृतिक भाषा विवरणों के आधार पर दृश्य में लक्ष्य वस्तुओं की स्थिति निर्धारित करने का प्रयास करता है। यह एम्बोडीड AI, रोबोटिक्स एवं मानव-दृश्य अंतःक्रिया के लिए एक मौलिक क्षमता है, जहाँ एजेंटों को भाषा, दृश्य रूप एवं स्थानिक संरचना पर एक साथ तर्क करना पड़ता है।
RePAIR, एक RAG Response-Action सीखने का पैरिडिगम, दोषपूर्ण RAG आउटपुटों को प्रभावी कार्यों में सीधे रूपान्तरित करता है, बिना विस्तृत त्रुटि वर्गीकरण या स्पष्ट आलोचक निगरानी पर निर्भरता के।
ट्रांसफॉर्मर आर्किटेक्चर (वास्वानी आदि द्वारा)
मॉडल की आंतरिक निश्चितता, अर्थात् इसकी आधारभूत प्रायिकता वितरण की केंद्रितता, एंकरिंग प्रतिरोध का एक विश्वसनीय निदानात्मक संकेत है।

इस पेपर में, हम संबंधों की जटिलता के आधार पर LLMs के RE कार्य में प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन करते हैं। इसके लिए, हम चार LLMs के स्तर-स्तर एवं दस्तावेज़-स्तर पर RE प्रदर्शन को एक ग्राफ-आधारित पार्सर के विभिन्न कॉन्फ़िगरेशन के साथ तुलना करते हैं।
इस कार्य में, हम LLMs को फाइन-ट्यूनिंग हेतु उपयोग करने हेतु ES का व्यापक प्रयोगात्मक विश्लेषण प्रस्तुत करते हैं, जिसका केंद्र निरंतर सीखने एवं भूलने पर है।
मिश्रित-सीमित समान टॉप-के नमूनाकरण।
हमने मॉडल को केवल लैमजाजुडिंग कार्य पर ही प्रशिक्षित किया, और फिर परिणामी मॉडलों का सीधे एंड-टू-एंड गणितीय मानकों पर मूल्यांकन किया, ताकि स्थानांतरण क्षमता का परीक्षण किया जा सके।

यह अध्ययन, हार्डवेयर-सचेतन सिमुलेशन का उपयोग करके, यह दर्शाता है कि एनालॉग शोर लगातार लेकिन कार्य एवं वास्तुकला-निर्भर प्रदर्शन में गिरावट लाता है; जिसका प्रभाव तर्क-संसाधन-आधारित कार्यों पर वाक्य-स्तर के वर्गीकरण कार्यों की तुलना में अधिक होता है। सबमॉड्यूल एवं ध्यान-स्तर के विश्लेषण से पता चलता है कि Q/K/V प्रोजेक्शन एवं प्रारंभिक ध्यान निर्माण सबसे संवेदनशील होते हैं, जबकि फीड-फॉरवर्ड लेयर अपेक्षाकृत अधिक मजबूत रहती हैं। इसके अलावा, एनालॉग अनुमानन एकसमान रूप से विफल नहीं होता, बल्कि ध्यान संरचना एवं संदर्भ-आधारित तर्क को नियंत्रित करने वाले विशिष्ट आंतरिक तंत्रों को बाधित करता है।
मल्टी-स्टेज LLM पाइपलाइन के लिए पुनरुत्पादन योग्य मूल्यांकन हेतु आवश्यक न्यूनतम आर्टिफैक्ट्स का समूह।
वर्तमान में, तर्कशीलता बड़े भाषा मॉडलों (LLM) के विकास में एक केंद्रीय लक्ष्य बन गई है (Xu et al.)।
MARCH (MultiAgent Radiology Clinical Hierarchy)

यह प्रदर्शित किया गया है कि प्रीफ़िक्स पार्सिंग, वास्तव में सामान्य पार्सिंग ही है—जो प्रीफ़िक्स व्याकरण पर लागू की जाती है, एवं यह प्रीफ़िक्स भाषा का एक संक्षिप्त CFG-आधारित प्रतिनिधित्व है। किसी भी CFG के लिए, हम एक नया CFG बनाते हैं, जिसका सामान्य पार्सर मूल CFG के प्रीफ़िक्स वेट्स की गणना करता है।
प्रस्तुत कार्य में, हम भाषाई सामग्री एवं बोलने वाले की जानकारी से प्रोसोडी को अलग करने हेतु एक स्पष्ट प्रोसोडी प्रतिनिधित्व का परिचय देते हैं।
L2T, एक प्री-ट्रेनिंग फ्रेमवर्क, जो मानक CLM के साथ भाषा सीखने के कार्य को एकीकृत करता है।
प्रशिक्षण डेटा मूल रूप से बड़े भाषा मॉडलों (LLMs) की क्षमता को निर्धारित करता है (Xu et al.)।

अत्यंत कम संसाधन वाले भाषाओं में मशीन अनुवाद की प्रदर्शन में अत्यधिक विविधता देखी गई है। हालिया अध्ययनों (Haddow et al. , 2022) से पता चलता है कि जबकि कुछ अफ्रीकी एवं प्राचीन भाषाओं में BLEU स्कोर 40 से अधिक हो सकते हैं, लेकिन समान परिस्थितियों में कुछ अमेरिकी या दक्षिण एशियाई मूलभूत भाषाओं को 5 से कम BLEU स्कोर प्राप्त करना कठिन है; अर्थात्, समान मात्रा में प्रशिक्षण डेटा के साथ किसी उच्च-संसाधन वाली भाषा में अनुवाद करते समय।

यह दस्तावेज़ LLMs के लिए सदस्यता अनुमानन के लिए सैद्धांतिक रूप से स्पष्ट मूल्यांकनों को विकसित करने में शोधकर्ताओं द्वारा सामना की गई चुनौतियों का सारांश प्रस्तुत करता है। इसके बाद, दो सामान्य खुले LLM परिवारों के लिए एक अधिक स्पष्ट डेटा विभाजन को लागू किया गया है, जिसे “ब्लाइंड बेसलाइन” के माध्यम से जाँचा गया है ताकि यह सुनिश्चित किया जा सके कि इस विभाजन में उन ही चुनौतियों का कोई प्रभाव न हो। अंत में, इन स्पष्ट विभाजनों पर कई सामान्य विधियों का मूल्यांकन किया गया है, जिससे उनकी प्रदर्शन क्षमता अधिक सीमित पाई गई।

इस अध्ययन में, हम लुर्इंग संदर्भों वाले कॉर्पस एवं साइबरगूमिंग कॉर्पस के बीच की सांख्यिकीय वितरण समानताओं को मापने हेतु विशेषता संरेखण विश्लेषण का उपयोग करते हैं। मॉडल सामान्यीकरण मूल्यांकन यह मापता है कि लुर्इंग संदर्भों वाले डेटा पर प्रशिक्षित मॉडल कितने प्रभावी रूप से साइबरगूमिंग पहचान में उपयोगी होते हैं।

बड़े भाषा मॉडल (LLMs) मानव-निर्धारित सुरक्षा नीतियों को लागू करने हेतु व्यापक संरेखण प्रशिक्षण से गुजरते हैं, जिससे गलत उपयोग, पूर्वाग्रह एवं हानिकारक आउटपुट से जुड़े जोखिम कम हो जाते हैं (केंटन आदि, 2021; मैथ्यूज़ आदि, 2022)।

निम्न-सटीकता तकनीकों पर हालिया अध्ययनों में व्यापक रूप से क्वांटीकरण एवं संपीड़न जैसे विधियों का उपयोग किया गया है, ताकि न्यूरल नेटवर्कों की दक्षता एवं स्केलेबिलिटी में वृद्धि हो सके एवं गणनात्मक लागत कम हो सके (नागेल आदि; कर्टिक आदि।

विज़न-भाषा मॉडल (VLMs) दृश्य सामग्री के पाठ्य वर्णन बनाने हेतु लगातार उपयोग में आ रहे हैं (ज़ांग आदि, 2024; वांग आदि, 2024; डीटिक आदि, 2025; गंधी आदि, 2023), जिसका असर अंधे, कम दृष्टि वाले एवं सामान्य दृष्टि वाले उपयोगकर्ताओं दोनों पर पड़ता है (मॉरिस आदि, 2016; ग्लीसन आदि, 2019; स्टैंगल आदि, 2020)।
यह दृष्टिकोण अक्सर “अति-भूलने” का परिणाम देता है, जहाँ अनावश्यक ज्ञान को हटाने से मॉडल की कुल प्रदर्शन क्षमता एवं उपयोगिता में स्पष्ट रूप से गिरावट आती है (Maini et al.)।
वैश्विक स्वास्थ्य संदर्भों में।
अनुमानात्मक तर्क (पीयरस, 1931; फ्रांकफर्ट, 1958) मानव बुद्धि का एक मूलभूत तत्व है, जो अवलोकन से सर्वोत्तम व्याख्यात्मक परिकल्पना तक पहुँचने वाली अनुमान प्रक्रिया को दर्शाता है।

यह फ्रेमवर्क तीन घटकों से बना है। सबसे पहले, हम संबंधित प्रभावों का नियंत्रित विश्लेषण करने हेतु तीन मूलभूत घटना संबंध प्रकारों—कारण-परिणाम, समय संबंध, एवं उप-घटना संबंधों—को शामिल करने वाला एक बड़े पैमाने पर विपरीत-उदाहरण डेटासेट बनाते हैं। दूसरे, हम विशिष्ट घटना संबंधों से मजबूती से जुड़े आंतरिक विशेषताओं की पहचान करने हेतु विरल ऑटो-एन्कोडर्स (SAEs) का उपयोग करते हैं। तीसरे, हम मॉडल के व्यवहार पर इन संबंध-संवेदनशील विशेषताओं के प्रभाव का अध्ययन मॉडल के हस्तक्षेप एवं प्रशिक्षण के माध्यम से करते हैं।
यह प्रस्तुत किया गया पहला कथा-संबंध डेटासेट है।

यह दस्तावेज़ अंग्रेजी-केंद्रित भाषा मॉडलों के लिए बहुभाषी संरेखण हेतु एक नवीन दृष्टिकोण प्रस्तुत करता है, जो टोकन विक्षेपण तकनीकों का उपयोग करता है। हमने भाषा-संवेदनशील टोकन बूस्टिंग (LATB) एवं इसके अनुकूलनशील रूप, एडाप्टिव-एलएटीबी का प्रस्ताव रखा है। व्यापक प्रयोगों से पता चला है कि हमारे विधियों से मूल मॉडल की तुलना में भाषा संबंधी भ्रम में काफी कमी आती है, एवं यह मॉडल के बहुभाषी रूप से अनुकूलित मॉडल से बेहतर प्रदर्शन करता है।
हालाँकि, इन तकनीकों के बावजूद, वे अक्सर हानिकारक (Khanov et al., 2024), अनचाहे (Wang et al., 2024), एवं पूर्वाग्रही (Li et al., 2025b) उत्तर उत्पन्न करती हैं।

इस लेख में, हम बुल्वर-लाइटन काल्पनिक प्रतियोगिता (BLFC) से उद्धृत वाक्यों के माध्यम से, एक कम अध्ययन की गई सांख्यिकीय हास्य शैली – अर्थात् जानबूझकर खराब हास्य – के लिए एक नई डेटासेट का परिचय देते हैं।

यह शोध दर्शाता है कि व्यक्तिगतकरण के माध्यम से सहानुभूति को बढ़ाने की कोशिश करने से अनजाने में सामाजिक असमानताएँ और भी बढ़ सकती हैं। उपयोगकर्ता की याददाश्त को मॉडल में शामिल करने से, विशेष रूप से लाभान्वित व्यक्तियों की तुलना में वंचित व्यक्तियों के लिए, भावनात्मक तर्क में लगातार परिवर्तन होता है।
यह कार्य, OC साथी एजेंटों के लिए एक न्यूरो-सिंबॉलिक एजेंटिक रीनफोर्समेंट लर्निंग फ्रेमवर्क (NSARL) के माध्यम से उपरोक्त कमी को दूर करता है।
गुणसमूह संबंधी नीति अनुकूलन (GRPO) (शॉ आदि द्वारा)

इस कार्य में, हम प्रॉक्सी-आधारित टेस्ट-टाइम एलाइनमेंट समस्या के लिए एक नया प्रायिकतात्मक ग्राफिकल मॉडल प्रस्तुत करते हैं, जिसे एक अस्वीकरण मानदंड (या वितरण) के माध्यम से पैरामीटराईकृत किया जा सकता है।
ग्राफ-आधारित रीट्रिवल ऑगमेंटेड जनरेशन (GraphRAG) (एज आदि द्वारा)

वर्तमान एजेंट प्रणालियाँ संवाद को योजना बनाने का एक परिणाम मानती हैं, जिसमें प्रणाली आंतरिक रूप से “तर्क” करती है, फिर भाषा के माध्यम से निष्कर्ष व्यक्त करती है। हम इस दृष्टिकोण का विपरीत रूप सुझाते हैं: कि संवाद योजना बनाने की प्रक्रिया का ही एक हिस्सा है। सहयोगात्मक परिस्थितियों में योजना बनाने की प्रक्रिया में एक मौलिक चुनौती होती है, जहाँ प्राकृतिक भाषा में निर्धारित लक्ष्य अस्पष्ट होते हैं, एवं कार्य शुरू करने से पहले इस अस्पष्टता को पूरी तरह हल करना असंभव होता है।

AI शोध को पुनरुत्पादित एवं पुनः उपयोग करने में कठिनाई होती है, क्योंकि इसका ज्ञान स्पष्ट नहीं होता एवं पाठ, कोड एवं कॉन्फ़िगरेशन में विखुरा हुआ होता है। इस चुनौती का समाधान करने हेतु, हम “एक्जिक्यूटेबल नॉलेज ग्राफ” (XKG) का प्रस्ताव करते हैं—यह एक नवीन, लेख-केंद्रित ज्ञान आधार है जो छिपी हुई वैज्ञानिक ज्ञान को सत्यापनीय एवं चालू रूप में परिवर्तित करता है।
SFT एवं RL के माध्यम से प्रशिक्षित “सिस्टम 2” मल्टीमोडल तर्क मॉडल (MRMs), चरण-दर-चरण तर्क प्रदान करने हेतु, गणितीय एवं तार्किक क्षेत्रों में उल्लेखनीय प्रगति का कारण बने हैं।

प्रोटीन, जिन्हें अच्छी तरह अध्ययन किया गया है, लाखों साहित्यिक स्रोतों एवं सैकड़ों संकलित डेटाबेसों में विश्लेषित किए जाते हैं।

यह शोध, शब्द-संरचित पाठ उत्पादन कार्य के माध्यम से गैर-ऑटोरेग्रेसिव (NAR) मॉडलों के डिकोडिंग स्पेस का अध्ययन करता है, जिसका उद्देश्य पूर्व-निर्धारित शब्दों वाले सबसे संभावित उत्पादन को खोजना है। ऑटोरेग्रेसिव (AR) मॉडलों की तुलना में, इसके लिए पहले से ही खोज-आधारित डिकोडिंग एल्गोरिदम उपलब्ध हैं। इसलिए, NAR मॉडलों के लिए समान खोज-आधारित डिकोडिंग एल्गोरिदम विकसित करके, हम समान शब्द-संरचित परिस्थितियों में AR एवं NAR डिकोडिंग की तुलना कर सकते हैं। विशेष रूप से, हम Directed Acyclic Transformer (DAT) पर आधारित शब्द-संरचित डिकोडिंग हेतु एक नई डायनामिक प्रोग्रामिंग (DP) एल्गोरिदम प्रस्तावित करते हैं।

Model Bahasa Besar (LLMs) telah meraih popularitas yang luar biasa dan menunjukkan kinerja yang sangat baik dalam berbagai tugas. Namun, penyesuaian model-model raksasa ini untuk tugas-tugas downstream tertentu tetap menjadi tantangan yang signifikan, terutama karena ukuran dan kebutuhan komputasi yang sangat besar. Untuk mengatasi hal ini, metode Parameter-efficient FineTuning (PeFT) muncul sebagai paradigma dominan.

Model Bahasa Besar (LLMs) telah meningkatkan berbagai tugas bahasa (Devlin et al., 2019; Radford et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2022b; Team et al., 2024; Touvron et al., 2023), namun pelatihan hanya menggunakan teks membuat mereka lemah dalam hal pengetahuan umum visual. Model Visi-Bahasa (VLMs) dilatih secara bersamaan menggunakan gambar dan teks (Alayrac et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023b, a; Li et al., 2023a; Dai et al., 2023; Cha et al., 2024), sehingga meningkatkan kemampuan berbasis visual.

Meskipun sederhana, desain ini sulit menangkap dinamika percakapan yang alami dan sering kali menimbulkan latensi. Sebaliknya, sistem dialog full-duplex memungkinkan mendengarkan dan berbicara secara bersamaan, sehingga interaksi menjadi lebih lancar dan alami.

Transformers (Vaswani et al., 2017) secara rutin menunjukkan adanya “attention sink”: kecenderungan yang persisten untuk mengalokasikan massa perhatian yang tidak proporsional pada posisi awal (sering kali posisi pertama), terlepas dari konten semantiknya (Xiao et al., 2024; Gu et al., 2025). Efek ini telah diamati pada berbagai tahap pelatihan dan hiperparameter (Gu et al., 2025; Guo et al., 2024), pada berbagai keluarga model dan dataset (Xiao et al., 2024), serta dengan berbagai skema encoding posisi—termasuk ALiBi (Press et al., 2022), RoPE (Su et al., 2023), dan bahkan tanpa skema encoding posisi yang eksplisit (Gu et al., 2025). Pola serupa juga telah dilaporkan pada model multimodal besar dan vision transformers (Kang et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Feng dan Sun, 2025).
Model-model CQF menunjukkan bias tidak hanya terhadap artikel bergaya Wikipedia, tetapi juga terhadap domain konten tertentu.

Penelitian ini menyajikan analisis kritis yang terpadu terhadap metode optimasi berbasis kelompok. Kami mengusulkan formulasi umum untuk metode bergaya GRPO, dengan menunjukkan sepuluh pendekatan terkini sebagai kasus khusus. Perspektif ini mengungkapkan masalah-masalah yang sama, yaitu bahwa tujuan pengganti sering kali didominasi oleh skema penimbangan, regularisasi, dan importance sampling, bukan oleh maksimisasi imbalan murni. Berdasarkan formulasi ini, kami mengidentifikasi tiga sifat yang berulang dalam dinamika pelatihan bergaya GRPO: (i) kami menganalisis gradien pada tingkat token untuk menunjukkan bahwa penimbangan yang tidak seragam menyebabkan bias sistematis pada token prefix yang sama; (ii) kami mempelajari interaksi dengan AdamW (Loshchilov dan Hutter, 2017), yang menunjukkan bahwa proses pelatihan tetap invarian terhadap penskalaan imbalan global dalam berbagai skenario; (iii) kami menunjukkan bahwa momentum optimizer dapat mendorong pembaruan kebijakan melampaui batas clipping yang direncanakan selama optimasi multi-langkah. Selain kinerja empiris, analisis kami memberikan wawasan teoretis yang mengungkapkan adanya perbedaan antara tujuan pengganti dan tujuan pelatihan yang sebenarnya. Dengan mengkarakterisasi dinamika-dinamika ini, temuan kami memberikan referensi bagi komunitas dalam merancang dan menafsirkan strategi pelatihan pasca-pelatihan LLM.

Sistem memori yang tahan lama sangat penting bagi agen model bahasa untuk mempertahankan koherensi dalam interaksi jangka panjang (Park et al., 2023). Selain mengingat fakta, dialog jangka panjang memerlukan penalaran mengenai ketergantungan temporal, rantai kausal, dan hubungan multi-hop antar giliran percakapan (Weller et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2025; Maharana et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2018). Hal ini memerlukan representasi memori yang mengorganisir peristiwa menjadi struktur yang berbasis waktu dan relasional (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019). Sistem memori yang ada umumnya terbagi menjadi dua paradigma, yaitu memori datar dan memori berbasis graf, yang menunjukkan adanya trade-off antara efisiensi dan penalaran terstruktur, seperti yang ditunjukkan pada Gambar 1.

3D visual grounding (3DVG) bertujuan untuk melokalisasi objek target dalam suatu adegan berdasarkan deskripsi bahasa alami. Ini merupakan kemampuan fundamental untuk AI yang terintegrasi dengan tubuh, robotika, dan interaksi manusia–lingkungan, di mana agen harus melakukan penalaran bersama atas bahasa, penampilan visual, dan struktur spasial.
Model bahasa besar (LLMs) mencapai kinerja generatif yang kuat, namun tetap rentan terhadap halusinasi fakta yang menghambat penerapan yang andal.

Meskipun teknik pasca-pelatihan seperti instruction tuning berhasil mengurangi banyak bias sosial dalam Large Language Models (LLMs), sistem-sistem ini tetap rentan terhadap bias kognitif yang diwarisi dari data yang dihasilkan manusia (Echterhoff et al., 2024). Contoh yang menonjol adalah efek anchoring (Tversky dan Kahneman, 1974), di mana penilaian kuantitatif dipengaruhi secara tidak proporsional oleh nilai awal yang tidak relevan. Penelitian sebelumnya telah menunjukkan adanya bias anchoring dalam LLMs (Nguyen, 2024; Lou dan Sun, 2024; Huang et al., 2025; Valencia-Clavijo, 2025), dan telah terbukti bahwa kerentanan terhadap anchoring bervariasi secara signifikan antar keluarga model dan paradigma pelatihan (Hagendorff et al., 2023; Lou dan Sun, 2024; Nguyen, 2024). Namun, belum ada cara yang kuat untuk memprediksi kapan sebuah model akan paling rentan terhadap bias anchoring.

Ekstraksi relasi (RE) merupakan tugas inti dalam NLP yang melibatkan ekstraksi triple RDF [kepala, relasi, dependen] (Candan et al., 2001) dari teks (Zhao et al., 2024). Dalam pengaturan terawasi, RE dapat didekati dengan berbagai model, dengan salah satu paradigma yang paling populer adalah parser berbasis graf (Verga et al., 2018; Tang et al., 2022). Meskipun literatur terkini telah mengeksplorasi kemampuan LLM autoregresif untuk melakukan RE melalui pembelajaran dalam konteks (Wan et al., 2023; Bi et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2024) serta pengawasan melalui pemodelan bahasa kausal (Zhang et al., 2024; Papaluca et al., 2024; Gajo dan Barrón-Cedeño, 2025), sejauh pengetahuan kami belum ada perbandingan langsung yang dilakukan antara keduanya dengan parser berbasis graf dalam pengaturan terawasi.

Meskipun kemajuan pesat dalam AI dengan LLM berbasis transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017; Brown et al., 2020; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2024), sebagian besar sistem state-of-the-art tetap statis setelah pelatihan dan tidak memiliki kemampuan untuk belajar secara terus-menerus selama proses deployment.
Pembelajaran relatif kelompok.

Model-model bahasa besar (LLMs) terkini mencapai skor tinggi dalam benchmark matematika dan sering kali dapat menghasilkan teks yang menyerupai pembuktian (Welleck et al., 2022; OpenAI et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2024; Shao et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025b; Guo et al., 2025). Namun, perilaku mereka sering kali mencerminkan peniruan pola daripada penalaran yang berprinsip: model cenderung mereproduksi jalur solusi yang familiar, dan mereka dapat mengadopsi kesimpulan dari sebuah lemma tanpa memvalidasi hipotesisnya. Perilaku semacam ini memanfaatkan korelasi permukaan dalam distribusi pelatihan dan melemahkan kepercayaan terhadap penalaran matematika.

Dalam sistem-sistem ini, hasil evaluasi yang dilaporkan tidak hanya bergantung pada model dasarnya, tetapi juga pada komponen-komponen perantara dan pilihan konfigurasi. Meskipun pelatihan sebelumnya dengan CLM memberikan pengetahuan dunia dan kemampuan umum pada LMs (Brown et al., 2020; Kojima et al., 2022), hal tersebut tidak mengoptimalkan kompetensi linguistik, yaitu kemampuan untuk memahami dan menafsirkan berbagai fenomena linguistik (Chomsky, 1965; Waldis et al., 2024). Akibatnya, LMs sering kali berperilaku seperti burung beo stokastik (Bender et al., 2021).

Cybergrooming melibatkan eksploitasi seksual terhadap anak-anak oleh orang dewasa di lingkungan digital (Wachs et al., 2012). Ini merupakan masalah sosial yang semakin parah, yang menyebabkan kerusakan psikologis serius dan potensi kerusakan fisik pada anak-anak yang rentan (Schittenhelm et al., 2025). Sistem deteksi cybergrooming otomatis (Inches dan Crestani, 2012) dapat membantu melindungi pengguna muda di platform digital, namun pengembangannya dibatasi oleh kelangkaan data dan batasan hukum, yang membatasi akses terhadap data pelatihan yang cukup untuk membangun model deteksi yang akurat (An et al., 2025a). Penelitian sebelumnya menunjukkan bahwa cybergrooming sering melibatkan penggunaan strategi komunikasi yang memikat (LCT) untuk memanipulasi anak-anak (Olson et al., 2007). Hal ini menimbulkan pertanyaan penting: Apakah model yang dilatih pada korpus komunikasi yang memikat yang tersedia secara publik dapat digeneralisasi ke berbagai domain untuk mendeteksi cybergrooming?

Model bahasa besar (LLMs) menjalani pelatihan penyesuaian yang ekstensif untuk menanamkan kebijakan keamanan yang didefinisikan oleh manusia, guna mengurangi risiko yang terkait dengan penyalahgunaan, bias, dan output yang berbahaya (Kenton et al.).

Penelitian terbaru mengenai teknik presisi rendah telah banyak dieksplorasi (misalnya, kuantisasi dan kompresi) untuk meningkatkan efisiensi dan skalabilitas jaringan saraf sambil mengurangi biaya komputasi (Nagel et al.; Kurtic et al.

Model bahasa besar (LLMs) dilatih menggunakan kumpulan data teks yang sangat besar, yang mungkin secara tidak sengaja mencakup informasi pribadi sensitif atau konten berhak cipta. Untuk mengatasi masalah ini, penelitian-penelitian terbaru telah mengeksplorasi konsep “unlearning” pada LLM, yaitu pendekatan pasca-pelatihan yang bertujuan untuk menghapus representasi yang disimpan atau dikodekan secara internal oleh model terhadap konten pribadi atau berhak cipta tertentu, tanpa perlu melatih ulang model dari awal.

Model bahasa besar (LLMs) semakin terintegrasi ke dalam alur kerja klinis, mulai dari komunikasi dengan pasien hingga dukungan pengambilan keputusan (Rajpurkar et al.). Namun, akurasi benchmark yang tinggi saja tidak menjamin penerapan yang aman. Dalam praktiknya, sistem klinis sering mengandalkan skor kepercayaan model untuk memprioritaskan kasus, memicu eskalasi, atau menyerahkan keputusan kepada dokter. Oleh karena itu, keandalan menjadi persyaratan utama: model harus akurat dan terkalibrasi dengan baik, sehingga tingkat kepercayaan yang lebih tinggi mencerminkan kemungkinan kebenaran yang lebih besar, dan sinyal kepercayaan mereka harus tetap stabil meskipun ada variasi input yang tidak berbahaya. Sektor kesehatan semakin memperparah kekhawatiran ini: jika petunjuk identitas sensitif secara sistematis memengaruhi keputusan klinis atau estimasi ketidakpastian, hal ini berisiko menyebabkan perawatan pasien yang tidak adil dan tidak aman.

Penalaran abduktif (Peirce, 1931; Frankfurt, 1958) merupakan fondasi kecerdasan manusia yang merujuk pada proses inferensi menuju hipotesis penjelasan terbaik berdasarkan pengamatan. Kemampuan ini sangat mendasar untuk tugas kognitif yang kompleks, mulai dari penalaran berdasarkan akal sehat hingga penemuan ilmiah (Bhagavatula et al., 2020; Bisk et al., 2019).

Hubungan antar peristiwa merepresentasikan ketergantungan semantik terstruktur antar peristiwa, seperti hubungan kausal, temporal, dan sub-peristiwa (Cheng et al., 2025). Dalam bahasa alami, hubungan semacam ini sering kali diekspresikan secara implisit lintas kalimat. Sebagai contoh, ketika sebuah narasi menyebutkan pemadaman listrik dan keterlambatan kereta api, hubungan yang bermakna dapat disimpulkan dari konteks tanpa adanya konjungsi eksplisit, seperti yang ditunjukkan pada Gambar 1.

Resolusi referensi silang tetap menjadi tugas yang menantang dalam pemrosesan bahasa alami, karena bergantung pada keputusan yang melampaui batas kalimat dan memerlukan konteks wacana lengkap serta pengetahuan dunia.

Model bahasa besar (LLMs) telah menunjukkan kinerja yang luar biasa, namun pengembangan yang berfokus pada bahasa Inggris membatasi efektivitasnya bagi pengguna non-Inggris (Hadi et al., 2024, 2023). Upaya-upaya terbaru (Xue et al., 2021; Workshop et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2023) bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kemampuan multibahasa, meskipun model yang berfokus pada bahasa Inggris tetap kurang efektif dalam bahasa-bahasa dengan sumber daya terbatas (Qin et al., 2024; OpenAI et al., 2024). Salah satu masalah utamanya adalah kebingungan bahasa (Devine, 2024), di mana model gagal menghasilkan bahasa yang diinginkan secara konsisten, terutama dalam konteks non-Inggris (Marchisio et al., 2024). Teknik-teknik untuk mengurangi masalah ini termasuk penurunan suhu, prompting dengan sedikit contoh, dan fine-tuning (Marchisio et al., 2024), namun teknik-teknik ini memiliki keterbatasan seperti berkurangnya keragaman respons (Agarwal et al., 2024; Renze dan Guven, 2024) atau peningkatan biaya komputasi.

Meskipun telah terjadi kemajuan signifikan, model-model ini sering kali menghasilkan respons yang merugikan (Khanov et al., 2024), tidak diinginkan (Wang et al., 2024), dan bias (Li et al., 2025b), akibat keterbatasan inherent dalam model, data pelatihan, dan instruksi. Namun, keselarasan yang lebih baik dengan harapan manusia merupakan persyaratan yang tak terelakkan dalam banyak skenario praktis (Ji et al., 2024). Meskipun pendekatan seperti Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) (Ouyang et al., 2022) telah berhasil mencapai kinerja keselarasan yang kuat, persyaratan fine-tuning-nya sering kali tidak layak secara komputasi. Secara umum, semua pendekatan konvensional yang menyelaraskan LLM melalui fine-tuning kesulitan memenuhi tuntutan skalabilitas.
